# T15-lang-formula-parse

**Goal.** Implement `parse_formula` (strict and relaxed) and `all_parses` in `src/dsdk/lang/formula_syntax.py`.

**Files to edit.** `src/dsdk/lang/formula_syntax.py` only (private helpers allowed). Do NOT edit any file under `tests/`, `fixtures/`, `lexer.py`, `errors.py`, or `src/dsdk/logic`. The module docstring is the spec (grammar, associativity, exact error offsets and expected-sets): read it and `tests/lang/test_formula_syntax.py` first.

**Done when.** `cd /home/user/dsdk && uv run pytest tests/lang/test_formula_syntax.py -q` passes (exit 0). Then run `cd /home/user/dsdk && uv run pytest -q tests/core tests/logic tests/test_reuse.py` and confirm it still passes.

**Depends on.** T09 (the tokenizer).

**Pitfalls.**
- Start with `toks = tokenize(text, FORMULA_KEYWORDS, keep_whitespace=True)` for BOTH modes (lexing first: LexError beats any ParseError). Relaxed mode then drops WS tokens: `[t for t in toks if t.kind != "WS"]`. Non-str is `TypeError`. Build formulas with `Var(tok.text)`, `Const(True/False)` for TRUE/FALSE tokens, `Not`, `And`, `Or`, `Implies`, `Iff` from `dsdk.logic`.
- Error helper: `ParseError(message, offset, expected)` with `offset = toks[i].start` if token `i` exists else `len(text)`, and `expected` a set of kind names exactly as in the docstring (`"END"` is a pseudo-kind meaning end of input).
- RELAXED: precedence climbing, ONE function `expr(min_prec)` plus one `prefix()` (a recursive-descent function per level uses too many frames: depth 200 must not raise RecursionError). Table: IFF (1, left), ARROW (2, RIGHT), BAR (3, left), AMP (4, left); `~` is a prefix operator whose operand is parsed with `expr(5)`. Loop: `left = prefix()`; while next token is a binary kind with `prec >= min_prec`: consume; `right = expr(prec + 1)` for left-assoc kinds but `expr(prec)` for ARROW; `left = Cls(left, right)`. `prefix()`: NAME/TRUE/FALSE -> atom; TILDE -> `Not(expr(5))`; LPAREN -> track paren depth, `inner = expr(0)`, require RPAREN; anything else (including end of input) -> ParseError with expected `{"LPAREN","TILDE","NAME","TRUE","FALSE"}`. After the top-level `expr(0)`, leftover tokens -> ParseError at that token; the expected set after a complete operand is `{"AMP","BAR","ARROW","IFF"}` plus `"RPAREN"` when inside an open parenthesis, or plus `"END"` at top level (a missing `)` at end of input uses the RPAREN variant).
- STRICT: an explicit stack machine over the WS-including token list (recursion would be fine for depth 200 only with 1-2 frames per level; a stack is simplest). Context frames: `("not",)` waiting for the operand of `(~`; `("left",)` waiting for the left operand of `(x op y)`; `("right", left_formula, op_kind)` waiting for the right operand. Loop: want a formula: NAME/TRUE/FALSE -> atom, then "complete"; LPAREN -> if the NEXT token is TILDE push `("not",)` and consume both, else push `("left",)` and want a formula whose error set (if wrong) is `{"TILDE","LPAREN","NAME","TRUE","FALSE"}` (only for the token immediately after a `(`; everywhere else a formula start has no TILDE). Complete(value): empty stack -> any remaining token is ParseError `{"END"}`, else done; `("not",)` -> require RPAREN (expected `{"RPAREN"}`), pop, wrap `Not`, complete again; `("right", l, op)` -> require RPAREN, pop, build `Cls(l, value)`, complete again; `("left",)` -> require a WS token whose text is exactly `" "` (else ParseError expected `{"WS"}` at that token, or at end of input), then an operator kind AMP/BAR/ARROW/IFF (else expected is that 4-set), then another exactly-" " WS (else `{"WS"}`), replace the frame by `("right", value, op)` and want a formula.
- Both modes must build the SAME tree for canonical text; strict must reject everything else: `(a)`, `a & b`, `~a`, double spaces, tabs, a trailing space (see the table STRICT_BAD in the tests for offsets).
- `all_parses(text)`: tokenize WITHOUT whitespace; the tokens must alternate atom, op, atom, ...; ParseError otherwise (a bad token at its start offset; a missing final atom or an empty input at `len(text)`). Atoms list `A[0..k]`, operators `ops[0..k-1]`, `ops[i]` sits between `A[i]` and `A[i+1]`. `go(lo, hi)` returns the list of all trees for atoms lo..hi: `[A[lo]]` if lo == hi, otherwise for `i` in `range(lo, hi)` (root operator index), for `l` in `go(lo, i)`, for `r` in `go(i + 1, hi)`: append `Cls(ops[i])(l, r)`. Memoize by `(lo, hi)`. The order of that loop nest is tested.

**Rules.** Use ONLY file reading/editing and Bash for pytest. Never create sessions, triggers, agents or remote resources. Do not run git commands that change state. Remove `raise NotImplementedError` only in the functions this task owns. Keep docstrings. No new dependencies. 2 attempts total.
